front: Preprocessing vs postprocessing — which one changes the stored data?
back: Preprocessing (gain, TGC, dynamic range, filtering) alters signals before storage. Postprocessing (gray-scale maps, colorization, edge enhancement) is applied after storage and can be changed non-destructively.

front: Effect of a lower dynamic range on the displayed image?
back: Higher contrast — fewer gray shades between black and white, more binary appearance.
Averages consecutive frames to reduce noise, at the cost of temporal resolution — motion appears blurred.
The process of interpolating radial (polar) beam-line data onto a rectangular pixel grid for display.

front: Which zoom improves resolution — read or write?
back: Write zoom (reacquires with more scan lines / pixels in the ROI). Read zoom only magnifies stored data.
